title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline applied to a single shared LLM candidate improves emulator-executable success versus accepting the ungated LLM output. Generation used gpt-5-mini; the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic, rule-based repair operator with repair_budget ≤1 (no extra LLM calls). Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We add two reviewer-requested, artifact-grounded details: (1) an aggregate difficulty-level distribution for the 200 confirmatory intents extracted from the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, SHA-256 eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a) and (2) a concise, auditable description of the single repaired episode including task identifier, validator violation code(s), deterministic repair rule applied, and before/after normalized-configuration artifact references. All prompts, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle.

sections.introduction:
Automating routine network-operations (NetOps) changes with large language models (LLMs) promises reduced manual effort but raises an operational-safety question: do LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to control planes? Prior work demonstrates intent-to-configuration prototypes and documents structured-output failures (missing commands, misordering, protected-field modification) and proposes mitigations such as retrieval-augmentation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool-augmentation. Despite these proposals, there is limited execution-grounded evidence quantifying the marginal benefit of applying a bounded deterministic repair to the same initial LLM candidate (a low-hosted-call operational estimand).

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that isolates the “repair-on-same-candidate” question by sharing a single initial LLM candidate across both arms (baseline ungated acceptance and guarded generate–verify–repair). The shared-candidate estimand is operationally relevant when hosted-model call budgets are constrained. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise algorithmic descriptions of the deterministic three-stage validator and the deterministic, rule-based repair operator used in the guarded pipeline; and (3) complete execution accounting and exact-test justification for small-discordant-pair inference.
sections.related_work: Research exploring LLMs for NetOps has produced three interlocking strands that motivate the present study. First, intent-to-configuration work demonstrates that LLMs can synthesize device CLI-like commands from natural-language intents but that structured-output errors are common without additional constraints (missing required commands, incorrect ordering, or violation of protected-field policies). Empirical prototypes and surveys document these failure modes and report prototype success under curated conditions (Nguyen et al., 2024 [doi:10.1002/nem.2313]). Second, mitigation approaches—RAG, live schema grounding, constrained/grammar-aware decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool augmentation—have reduced hallucination in adjacent domains; these methods require careful adaptation to device CLI dialects. Third, deterministic formal verification and emulator-based validators (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers) provide natural assurance layers but have limits when modeling dynamic control-plane behaviors. Prior work calls for workflow-centered, execution-grounded benchmarks; our study targets a specific empirical gap by measuring the marginal yield of a bounded deterministic repair applied to the same initial candidate.
sections.methodology:
Design and preregistration: The confirmatory protocol (cnd-001-5f3a) is a paired, shared-initial-generation design. For each of n=200 curated intents the hosted model produced one initial candidate which was (A) scored directly (baseline) and (B) also passed to the guarded pipeline. The guarded pipeline executed a deterministic validator and, if the violation family was preregistered as repairable and uniquely mappable, invoked a deterministic rule-based repair operator (repair_budget ≤1). The primary estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline); the preregistered primary test is the exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage calls = 1).

Task bank and scoring: The task bank contains 200 intent–expected-configuration pairs created by a deterministic generator. Each task includes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, workflow_policies, and a difficulty label (easy/medium/hard/very_hard). The scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) requires syntactic parse, presence and ordering of required_sequence, dependency/group-policy compliance, preservation of protected interfaces, and emulator-observed final_state equality with expected_final_state. Provider/API generation failures are treated per the preregistered missingness plan as arm failures; none occurred.

Validator and repair operator: The deterministic validator executes three stages: (1) syntactic parsing and canonical normalization; (2) structural and workflow checks that emit deterministic violation codes (e.g., MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, TRANSIENT_ORDER_VIOLATION); (3) deterministic emulator application producing validation_after.valid. The repair operator is deterministic code (no LLM calls), invoked only for violation families with a unique mapping to a canonical transformation derived from the task manifest. The operator implements insertion (of missing required commands at canonical positions), reordering (stable minimal block moves to satisfy dependency constraints), and preservation enforcement (restoring protected-values from initial_state). Ambiguous cases cause abstention (no edit) and remain guarded failures. All validator and repair traces are archived for audit.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes: The confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 pairs) with no provider/API failures. Condition-level artifact-backed counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv) show baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Exact-test and CI: The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs) computed on the observed discordant count n = 1 yields p = 1.0 (analysis/results.json). Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) yielding [0.0, 0.015]. Because the preregistered primary effect-size target (absolute 0.15) lies well outside the observed CI, the confirmatory data do not support that magnitude under the shared-candidate estimand.

Reviewer-requested artifact-grounded additions (difficulty summary and repaired-episode exemplar):
1) Aggregate difficulty-label distribution (extracted from the archived task manifest execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a): easy = 30, medium = 78, hard = 68, very_hard = 24 (total = 200). This distribution documents a confirmatory bank skewed toward medium–hard tasks and was used in the preregistered power assessment and difficulty stratifications (the full manifest is archived for inspection). 

2) Single repaired episode (auditable exemplar): the one guarded-only conversion corresponded to task_id task-000137 (pair_id pair-000137) — the validator reported violation_codes = ["MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND"] and repair_applied = true. The deterministic repair rule applied was Insertion (canonical insertion of the missing required_sequence step derived from the task manifest). Before repair the normalized_configuration (shared_initial_candidate) is archived at execution/responses/task-000137-shared-initial.txt (SHA-256: 2ab3f7c4... [artifact archived]); after repair the normalized_configuration is archived at execution/scoring/task-000137-guarded.json (validator_trace.normalized_configuration) and the single repair trace is archived at execution/repairs/task-000137-repair.json (all repair-trace artifacts appear in the evidence bundle). (Readers may inspect these artifacts directly; the repair trace shows the deterministic insertion location and the inserted command derived from required_sequence. All artifact hashes and manifest entries are archived in the execution manifest.)

Repair and failure-accounting diagnostics: The validator reported initial validation_before.valid == false in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1 and that repair converted the episode to validator-passing. Syntactic/parse failures = 0. Provider-call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution/model_configuration.json) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}.

Interpretation: Under the shared-candidate estimand and this curated bank the conservative deterministic repair produced a single low-churn, auditable correction; with a near-ceiling baseline the marginal yield was therefore small. The CI excludes large preregistered absolute effects (0.15) under this estimand.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: Deterministic validators provide auditable structured failure codes that enable targeted rule-based repairs; in low-error regimes the marginal yield of a conservative deterministic repair on the same candidate is small but auditable and low-cost. For operators constrained by model-call budgets, the guarded shared-candidate design preserves low hosted-call cost while offering assurance. Where maximal pass rates are required, independent-resampling or LLM-guided iterative repair (at higher provider cost and audit burden) are alternative strategies.

Threats to validity and reviewer-requested formal note on power: Internal validity is high for the paired estimand and deterministic scoring. Construct validity depends on emulator fidelity—our deterministic emulator models control-plane state deterministically but cannot capture certain runtime dynamics (e.g., BGP convergence timing, vendor firmware idiosyncrasies). External validity is limited by a single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic curated bank. Critically, the preregistered power calculation assumed baseline ≈0.5 and targeted a 0.15 absolute effect at n=200; the observed baseline ≈0.995 compressed discordant counts (observed discordants n = 1), substantially reducing sensitivity to detect large absolute effects under the shared-candidate estimand. This is an explicit post-hoc limitation: with only one discordant pair the exact McNemar test is the appropriate small-sample test, but it offers limited power for the preregistered target effect-size given the realized baseline. The paired-bootstrap CI quantifies the practical uncertainty ([0.0, 0.015]).

Design-space trade-offs: Execution accounting (model_calls_used = 201; repairs invoked = 1) supports cost-versus-yield comparisons. Shared-candidate guarding is attractive where hosted-call budgets or audit constraints dominate; independent-resampling or multi-call repairs may be preferable when operators accept higher cost for higher pass rates. Deterministic validators should be considered mandatory assurance machinery in auditable NetOps deployments.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the baseline was near-ceiling. For this estimand and task distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded negligible marginal improvement, but deterministic validators remain valuable, auditable assurance gates for operational NetOps pipelines. Full artifacts and analysis code are archived in the evidence bundle for independent audit and re-analysis.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, research-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: generation requested gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json). Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock) include: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle.
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the archived evidence bundle (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a); the manuscript includes an aggregated summary extracted from that manifest.
